A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf C$ be a [[Definition:Metacategory|category]].
An object $T$ is [[Definition:Terminal Object|terminal]] {{iff}} for every object $X$ there is exactly one morphism $X \to T$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\mathbf C$ be a [[Definition:Metacategory|category]].
An object $I$ is [[Definition:Initial Object|initial]] {{iff}} for every object $X$ there is exactly one morphism $I \to X$.

object_map.reformulation: Pass to the opposite category C^op (reverse every morphism).

validity_conditions: C^op is a well-defined category (always true).
Op is an involution: (C^op)^op = C, so the dual of the dual returns the original.
proof_plan: Form $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$ by reversing all morphisms.
An initial object of $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$ has exactly one morphism to every object of $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$.
Reversing back, this is an object with exactly one morphism from every object of $\mathbf C$.

Hence $T$ is terminal in $\mathbf C$ {{iff}} $T$ is initial in $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$.
{{qed}}
